source_refs.note: Topic 5.5.1.5 Boxplots (PDF 148, printed 145). Figure 5.8 is described in the text; the original diagram uses the chapter's Class A and Class B scores.

blocks.text: Boxplots, or box-and-whisker plots, summarize a distribution by showing the median, the quartiles and possible outliers, giving a visual summary of variability. They are useful for comparing groups, such as the exam scores of different classes.

blocks.alt: Horizontal box plot titled Box Plot of Exam Scores for Three Classes, Exam Scores 50 to 100. Class 1: box about 62 to 75, median about 69, one high outlier. Class 2: box about 68 to 78, median about 73, two high outliers. Class 3: box about 72 to 85, median about 77, one low and one high outlier.
blocks.caption: Figure 5.8: A Boxplot, showing class scores performance of three classes (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 5.8).
